summary: Request: sampled audit correlation map and SIEM onboarding checklist for multi-tenant activity logs
description: Issue summary: Customer requests a compact, sampled audit correlation map plus a SIEM onboarding checklist for Fincrest Bank's pilot integration. Impact: They need a deterministic sampled export to validate cross-system joins (user_id->session_id->request_id) for compliance and fraud analytics without shipping full-volume logs. Goal is to provide example payloads, recommended ECS/EK mappings, HMAC manifest approach for sample batches, and a checklist for configuration in Splunk/Graylog/Elastic. Environment: Production tenant for Fincrest (multi-tenant; retention 90 days; VPC egress allowed to their ingestion endpoints in us-east).
steps_to_reproduce: N/A - this is a data-delivery and onboarding request rather than a bug.
Customer wants an export sample and mapping to validate downstream correlation and retention expectations.
Support to provide sample files (ndjson) and an onboarding checklist for SIEM ingestion.
required_deliverables: Deterministic sampled audit file (ndjson) covering 24h window, sample rate 1% with seed and resume token
Per-batch manifest (signed HMAC) with batch_start, batch_end, event_count, sample_seed
Field correlation map (CSV) showing canonical field -> recommended SIEM/ECS field
SIEM onboarding checklist for Splunk HEC, Graylog GELF, and Elasticsearch Ingest pipeline
Pseudonymization options and example transforms for customer PII fields
sample_field_mapping: user_id -> user.id (pseudonymize with HMAC if requested)
logs: No application error logs attached. This ticket is for dataset/sample delivery. Customer attached a short ingestion failure screenshot to the portal (refer to comment).
investigation_notes: Suggested deterministic sampling using seed-based hashing on event.uuid to produce stable 1% sample across exports.
SRE note: we can generate sample bundles via /exports/sampled endpoint with resume token and HMAC manifest; rate-limits apply - recommend scheduled 1x/hour export slices to avoid throttling.

Privacy: recommended to pseudonymize user.email and user.name using tenant-specific HMAC with KEK split; Fincrest requested reversible pseudonymization option via escrow (enterprise-only) - engineering to confirm availability.
ECS mapping drafted; need customer confirmation on preferred target (Splunk/ECS vs Elastic-native fields).
